pull_requests.title: ci(agent-ticket): force tag mode with track_progress so the agent get…
pull_requests.author: UBayouski
pull_requests.description:
The first automated run on issue #4 reported success after 19 turns with no branch, no
  comment, and no commit. Passing a `prompt` put claude-code-action in agent mode, which does
  not fetch the issue, create a branch, post a tracking comment, or allow git add/commit/push.
  Our prompt told the agent to read the issue it was triggered from, and it had neither the
  issue number nor a tool to get it.

  Changes:

  - `agent-ticket.yml`: `track_progress: true` forces tag mode on issue events. Tag mode fetches
    the issue, creates the `agent/issue-<n>-<slug>` branch, posts a progress comment, allows the
    git commands, and appends our prompt as custom instructions.
  - `agent-ticket.yml`: `Edit` and `Write` removed from the allow-list. Tag mode already permits
    edits inside the workspace; listing them would allow writes anywhere on the runner.
  - Both workflows: `actions/checkout@v5` and `actions/setup-node@v5`, clearing the Node 20
    deprecation warning.
  - `journal/day-04.md`: run log for the three attempts (zombie run during the GitHub Actions
    incident, missing Claude GitHub App, the agent-mode no-op) and what each needed from a human.

  No product code changes.

pull_requests.author: UBayouski
pull_requests.description:
Day 4: automate the factory's first job.

  - `.github/workflows/agent-ticket.yml`: adding the label `ready-for-agent` to an issue runs
    claude-code-action with a fixed prompt. The agent reads AGENTS.md and the issue, implements,
    runs `npm run check` (three attempts), and commits on `agent/issue-<n>-<slug>`. Guard rails:
    max 40 turns, 30-minute timeout, one run per issue. It does not open the PR; a human does.
  - `.github/workflows/agent-fix.yml`: an `@claude` comment on a PR pushes fixes to that branch
    for Qodo re-review.
  - `tickets/T-026`: the small ticket for the first automated run (print usage instead of blocking
    when stdin is a terminal). Mirrored as issue #4.
  - `tickets/T-003`: grouping ticket, written on Day 3, not yet implemented.
  - `AGENTS.md`: process rule amended. Bot commits are allowed only on `agent/*` branches created
    by the workflow; a human opens the PR and merges.
  - `journal/day-04.md`: skeleton with trigger design, run log to follow.

  No product code changes. `npm run check` unaffected.

pull_requests.title: feat: parse git log streams from stdin (T-002)
pull_requests.author: UBayouski
pull_requests.description:
## Day 3: feed your agent a ticket

  Implements `tickets/T-002-read-git-log-stream.md`: parse a `git log` stream from stdin into commits with SHA, author, date, and a parsed message. Nine acceptance criteria, written before implementation. The agent built it from the ticket text
  and `AGENTS.md` only.

  ### What's in the change
  - `src/gitlog.ts`: `parseGitLog`. Splits on the record and field separators, validates SHAs, keeps dates as strings with an ISO 8601 shape warning. Invalid SHAs and short records go to a `malformed` list with a reason. `count` always equals
  `commits + malformed`, so nothing in the range is dropped silently.
  - `src/cli.ts`: `tracenotes log` reads the stream from stdin and prints JSON. Exit 0 even with malformed records, exit 2 on empty stdin.
  - `tests/gitlog.test.ts`, `tests/cli.test.ts`: 11 new tests, one per criterion plus edge cases. Two fixtures under `tests/fixtures/`, marked binary in `.gitattributes` so the LF policy leaves the control bytes alone.
  - README: "From git history" section with the pipe command.
  - `journal/day-02.md`: records the Review Standards import (14 rules from AGENTS.md).
  - `journal/day-03.md`: criterion-by-criterion comparison and what the agent missed.

  ### Verification
  `npm run check` passes, 44 tests. The repository's own history piped through `tracenotes log` returns 7 commits and 0 malformed records, from both Git Bash and PowerShell 5.1.

  ### Result against the ticket
  9 of 9 criteria met. The gaps were in the ticket, not the code: it never mentioned the framing newline git prints between records, and it left separator collisions inside a message undefined. Both are documented in the journal.

pull_requests.title: feat: parse Conventional Commits messages (T-001)
pull_requests.author: UBayouski
pull_requests.description:
## Day 1: first delivery

  Implements `tickets/T-001-parse-conventional-commit.md`: parse one Conventional Commits
  message into structured data.

  ### What's in the change
  - `src/commit.ts`: parser following Conventional Commits 1.0.0. Type, scope, subject,
    breaking flag (`!` or `BREAKING CHANGE` footer), body, footers, breaking notes,
    issue references, and PR number from squash-merge subjects. Never throws on string input;
    non-conventional messages are returned with `conventional: false`.
  - `src/cli.ts`: `tracenotes parse <message>` or stdin. JSON output. Exit 2 on empty input
    or unknown command.
  - `tests/commit.test.ts`: 24 tests, one group per acceptance criterion.
  - Toolchain: Node 24 native TypeScript, `node --test`, `tsc --noEmit`. Zero runtime dependencies.

  ### Verification
  `npm run check` (typecheck + tests) passes locally.

  ### Acceptance criteria
  See the ticket. All eight are covered by tests; criterion 8 (CLI behaviour) was also
  checked by hand.
